title: Baptism
description: A lesson on the importance, meaning, and practice of baptism as an act of obedience for every believer.

cards.heading: Baptism: An Act of Obedience
cards.scriptureText: Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.
cards.body: God has given two ordinances to the Church: baptism and the Lord’s Supper. For a new believer, baptism is the first step of obedience. It is not optional—it is a command that every Christian should follow.
cards.question: Do you see baptism as optional or as an important step of obedience? Why?

cards.heading: The Importance of Baptism
cards.scriptureText: We were therefore buried with him through baptism into death in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead... we too may live a new life.
cards.body: Baptism is important because it follows the example of Jesus, obeys His command, and serves as a testimony of His sacrifice. It also represents the new life that has already taken place in the believer’s heart.
cards.question: What does baptism represent in your personal faith journey?

cards.heading: The Meaning of Baptism
cards.scriptureText: For all of you who were baptized into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ.
cards.body: Baptism is not simply a ritual like infant sprinkling. It is a picture of Christ’s death, burial, and resurrection. It also shows that the believer has died to sin and now lives a new life in Christ.
cards.question: How does understanding the meaning of baptism change your view of it?

cards.heading: Who Should Be Baptized
cards.scriptureText: Those who accepted his message were baptized...
cards.body: Only those who truly believe in Jesus Christ and have experienced new life should be baptized. Baptism follows personal faith and repentance, not tradition or age.
cards.question: Have you personally made a decision to follow Christ before considering baptism?

cards.heading: The Mode of Baptism
cards.scriptureText: As soon as Jesus was baptized, he went up out of the water.
cards.body: Biblical baptism is by immersion—being fully submerged in water. This reflects the original meaning of the word 'baptize' and clearly symbolizes death, burial, and resurrection.
cards.question: Why do you think immersion is an important symbol in baptism?

cards.heading: Baptism Does Not Save
cards.scriptureText: For it is by grace you have been saved, through faith... not by works, so that no one can boast.
cards.body: Baptism does not save a person. Salvation comes by grace through faith in Jesus Christ. Baptism is the outward expression of an inward change that has already taken place.
cards.question: Why is it important to understand that baptism does not save?

cards.heading: Application: A Step of Faith
cards.scriptureText: Do not merely listen to the word, and so deceive yourselves. Do what it says.
cards.body: A true believer should follow the Lord in baptism as a step of obedience. It is a public testimony of faith and a sign of being identified with the body of Christ.
cards.question: If you have not been baptized yet, what is stopping you from taking this step?
